reason: The first defective interaction is the note's purported primitiveVertex v / sharedLocalBuffer canonical-kind case. For any two distinct demands with v in both localBuffer sets, DemandActivation.localBuffer_subset_declaredSupport puts v in both declared supports. Thus CarrierItem.vertex v is a shared item and sharedDeclaredSupport (.vertex v) is a blocker of that same pair. The canonicalBlocker candidate list tests every sharedDeclaredSupport item before any sharedLocalBuffer item, with every vertex in orderedVertices. Consequently the canonical blocker can never have kind sharedLocalBuffer on any such pair; indeed any selected sharedLocalBuffer blocker would already have an earlier declared-support blocker. capacityRole uses the canonical kind, so a roleFibre with r.blocker = sharedLocalBuffer is empty. The proposed conclusion that primitiveVertex v with this kind places v in both actual T(p) supports is only a vacuous conditional, yet the result and note present it as a live original-pair/physical-support interaction and leave its geometry as an unresolved subobligation. Role-fibre membership does support a fixed canonical charge and role, and the first three token cases describe support containment, but they do not repair this false live-case premise. The result's phrase 'fixed canonical blocker carrier' also exceeds the first three cases, which select support incidences or a vertex and need not equal Blocker.carrier. Reject this task and inventory a nonvacuous canonical-kind case. All submitted evidence hashes match the live files.
